projects.name: DepthForge
projects.summary: DepthForge is a CUDA-accelerated implementation of the Semi-Global Matching algorithm for stereo depth estimation. It processes rectified stereo image pairs entirely on the GPU, delivering dense disparity maps with 1.78 px MAE and a 30× speedup over CPU baselines.
approach: Census Transform with 9×7 binary descriptor per pixel
Cost volume computation using Hamming distance and __popcll intrinsic
8‑path SGM aggregation using shared memory, parallel min‑reduction and atomicAdd
Winner‑Takes‑All disparity selection via argmin across disparity dimension
3×3 sorting‑network median filtering to suppress impulse noise
Jet colormap visualization converting disparity to RGB heatmap
CUDA kernel optimization and memory hierarchy tuning for KITTI‑resolution images
results: MAE: 1.784 px
RMSE: 6.884 px
Median error: 0.708 px
30× speedup over CPU baseline on synthetic 640×480 benchmark (48.064 ms vs 1440.6 ms)
Median processing time 168 ms on NVIDIA RTX 3050 Laptop GPU for KITTI‑resolution images

projects.name: ForgetField — Adaptive Hopfield Memory with Dynamic Pattern Forgetting
projects.summary: ForgetField introduces Adaptive Hopfield Memory with Dynamic Pattern Forgetting (AHM‑DPF), a neural‑network architecture that augments associative memory with feedback‑driven adaptation and selective forgetting to mitigate limited capacity and catastrophic interference in sequential pattern learning. The system learns a hidden representation, uses a feedback signal derived from previous training loss to adapt regularization, and achieves up to 99.8% evaluation accuracy on the BitPatternSet benchmark.
projects.problem: Classical Hopfield networks have limited storage capacity and can suffer from spurious attractors and interference when patterns are learned sequentially.
approach: Learned hidden representation for binary input patterns
Modern Hopfield‑style associative memory mechanism
Internal state conditioned on previous training performance
Feedback signal derived from the previous epoch's training loss (f_t = L_train(t−1))
Adaptive regularization behavior influenced by the feedback signal
Classification projection producing output logits
Combined classification and regularization objective
results: 99.8% final evaluation accuracy (AHM‑DPF Large)
0.043 final evaluation loss (AHM‑DPF Large)
100% best evaluation accuracy (AHM‑DPF Large)
87.3% final evaluation accuracy (AHM‑DPF Fair)
0.280 final evaluation loss (AHM‑DPF Fair)
88.3% best evaluation accuracy (AHM‑DPF Fair)
56.4% final accuracy for standard Hopfield Base model
Adaptive variants outperformed non‑adaptive counterparts by approximately 25–33 percentage points

projects.name: Network Intrusion Anomaly Detection Using Machine Learning
projects.summary: Developed a dual‑paradigm network intrusion detection framework that combines supervised learning for known attacks and unsupervised anomaly detection for zero‑day threats using the UNSW‑NB15 benchmark.
projects.problem: Detect both known and previously unseen network threats.
approach: Implemented supervised models: Random Forest, LightGBM, XGBoost, Logistic Regression
Implemented unsupervised methods: Isolation Forest, One-Class SVM
Applied SMOTE oversampling with 0.3 sampling strategy to reduce class imbalance from 19.67:1 to ~3.33:1
Performed PCA dimensionality reduction to 25 components retaining 92.87% variance
Conducted feature selection, missing‑value analysis, correlation analysis, data leakage prevention, stratified train/test split, and class imbalance analysis
results: Random Forest achieved 99.47% accuracy and 99.47% F1
LightGBM 99.41% accuracy, 99.41% F1
XGBoost 99.34% accuracy, 99.35% F1
Logistic Regression 98.55% accuracy, 98.64% F1
Random Forest class‑specific: normal precision 99.79%, normal recall 99.65%, normal F1 99.72%; attack precision 93.30%, attack recall 95.96%, attack F1 94.61%
One-Class SVM achieved 0.858 ROC‑AUC, 100% recall of test attacks, 28.4% false‑positive rate
Isolation Forest achieved 0.585 AUC

projects.name: Adversarial Robustness of Deep Learning-Based Network Intrusion Detection Systems
projects.summary: This project studies the adversarial robustness of a deep neural network‑based Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) trained on the UNSW‑NB15 dataset. It investigates whether small perturbations to network‑flow features can cause the NIDS to misclassify malicious traffic and explores defenses such as ε‑randomized PGD adversarial training.
projects.problem: Assess whether an attacker can manipulate network‑flow features by small perturbations to cause the DNN‑based NIDS to misclassify malicious traffic and improve its robustness.
approach: Implemented a fully‑connected IDS‑DNN with four hidden layers (42→256→128→64→32) using ReLU and dropout
Applied categorical encoding, min‑max normalization, targeted SMOTE, and class‑weighted loss during preprocessing
Evaluated the baseline model with FGSM and PGD attacks across six perturbation budgets (ε ∈ {0.00,0.01,0.05,0.10,0.20,0.30})
Trained a robust model using ε‑randomized PGD adversarial training with ε sampled from [0.01,0.15] and a weighted combination of clean and adversarial losses
Analyzed feature attribution with SHAP DeepExplainer and visualized penultimate‑layer representations with t‑SNE
results: Baseline macro F1 on clean data: 0.406; weighted F1: 0.709
Under PGD ε=0.10, baseline macro F1 dropped to 0.074 (81.7% reduction)
Robust model macro F1 at ε=0.10: 0.240 (223.8% recovery over baseline)
Weighted F1 improved from 0.257 to 0.553 with adversarial training
Robust model produced tighter and better‑separated t‑SNE clusters for several traffic classes
SHAP analysis showed the robust model distributed attribution more broadly across volume and timing features

projects.name: ARC-Nodule
projects.summary: ARC-Nodule is an acquisition‑robust lung‑nodule detection and malignancy‑classification pipeline that combines physics‑simulated CT augmentation, an anisotropy‑aware 3D Swin Transformer encoder, and cross‑acquisition consistency distillation to improve robustness to slice thickness, dose, and reconstruction‑kernel variations without requiring labeled data from the target protocol. It is built as a fully standalone package to address the failure of standard detectors under thicker‑slice acquisitions.
projects.problem: Nodule detectors are typically trained on thin‑slice CT (≤2.5 mm) and perform poorly on thicker slices (3–10 mm), with sensitivity dropping dramatically (e.g., 45.2%→26.2% at 5 mm). ARC‑Nodule targets this acquisition‑protocol shift by acting on the network’s internal representation rather than only on label mapping.
approach: Physics‑Simulated Acquisition Augmentation (PSAA) – deterministic transform that simulates thicker slices and dose noise without new annotations
Anisotropy‑aware Swin Transformer encoder – 3D Swin‑style backbone conditioned on voxel spacing via FiLM injection per attention block
Cross‑Acquisition Consistency Distillation (CACD) – consistency loss between degraded‑scan and native‑resolution passes with magnitude‑balancing TermBalancer
results: Validated, replicated finding: combining PSAA augmentation with the spacing‑conditioned encoder reduces thickness‑induced CPM drop from 33.1% to 21.6% at 5 mm and from 70.2% to 59.5% at 10 mm, improving in 9/9 seed‑by‑thickness cells with no cost to native thin‑slice detection
Unresolved finding: the CACD module has not yet beaten a matched no‑consistency control on its pre‑registered criterion; a properly powered, pre‑registered retest is planned
next_steps: Execute a properly powered, pre‑registered retest of the CACD module
Evaluate the pipeline on real thick‑slice scans from the LIDC‑IDRI validation arm

projects.name: Lepton — Rain-to-Traffic Impact Prediction and Analysis
projects.summary: Lepton is a production rain‑to‑road‑traffic analytics platform that quantifies and predicts how rainfall degrades traffic at individual‑road granularity across ten Indian cities. It provides both retrospective analytics and predictive forecasts (week‑ahead forecast and hour‑ahead nowcast) via an end‑to‑end data system with weather ingest, cross‑database joins, model families, and operational dashboards.
projects.problem: Naive "rain slows traffic" analytics fail on real municipal data for three reasons: (1) baseline contamination – raw slowdown during rain is mostly rush hour, so Lepton measures delay relative to each road's own median dry‑hour delay; (2) spatio‑temporal misalignment – traffic and weather timestamps differ, requiring bucketed joins to the IST clock hour; (3) rain‑source disagreement – precipitation products disagree, leading to a switch to ERA5‑Land as the default historical rain source.
approach: Weather ingest layer normalising ERA5, ERA5‑Land, NASA IMERG, Google Weather, and Open‑Meteo to a common hourly per‑H3‑cell precipitation schema with latency handling.
Retrospective analytics including a rain vulnerability builder with jackknife gating, rain network propagation graph analysis, flood impact isolation, and PDF reporting of top‑N rain bottlenecks.

Predictive models: weighted log‑linear regression forecast v2 with conformalized quantile regression severity bounds, and nowcast v2–v4 blending spateGAN‑derived rain fields and 15‑minute traffic panels with adaptive serve gating.
Serving layer of three dependency‑free http.server dashboards providing HTML and JSON APIs, orchestrating forecast and nowcast jobs as subprocesses.
Cross‑database ETL joining three PostgreSQL/PostGIS instances via pandas, using baseline‑relative traffic metrics and H3 geospatial indexing.
results: Retrospective builder reproduced live production bottleneck report road‑for‑road (151/151 qualifying roads, 33/33 storm‑dependent tier, top‑road excess delay 0.3% delta).
Forecast model v2 achieved +14.2% wet‑row skill vs naive (MAPE 7.67% vs 8.94%) and +19.2% skill with spateGAN rain fields.
Nowcast v4 blend reduced +15 min MAE by ~26% and +30 min MAE by ~15%; quantile coverage improved to ~0.90 after conformal calibration.
Propagation and flood products passed 3/3 verification tests, yielding 3.7× alert lift for propagation windows and 4.4× for flood windows.
Network amplification measured at 5.92 with spillover share 0.83; 73 robust source roads account for ~17% of total wet‑hour excess delay, while 329 surprise receivers absorb remaining spillover.

projects.name: PortfolioAI — Resume-Based Portfolio Chatbot and Job-Match Web App
projects.summary: PortfolioAI is a full‑stack LLM‑powered portfolio assistant that recruiters and hiring managers can chat with to learn about a candidate’s technical background. It grounds answers in the resume and detailed project write‑ups, and can score a candidate’s fit for a job description and generate a cover‑letter style verdict.
approach: Implemented a LangGraph state graph with one LLM node and three tool nodes (build_profile, parse_documents, match_profile)
Used a cached profile.json with SHA‑256 hashes to avoid rebuilding the profile on every request
Added per‑tool retry limits and failure classification (transient, unclear, precondition)
Built a FastAPI backend that streams token‑by‑token answers via Server‑Sent Events
Created a single‑page HTML/CSS/JavaScript frontend with file upload and live status UI
Provided a terminal client for command‑line interaction
Integrated LangSmith tracing for live chat observability
results: Version 2 built and deployed publicly, replacing version 1
Reduced cold‑start time from ~3.5 minutes to milliseconds by eliminating thirteen model calls at startup
Live recruiter chats are traced to LangSmith for inspection

projects.name: Video Transcript RAG — Lecture and Media Question Answering System
projects.summary: Video Transcript RAG is a retrieval-augmented question-answering pipeline for video or lecture content that converts media into searchable transcript chunks, stores them in a vector database, and answers user questions using only retrieved transcript context.
approach: Media-to-audio conversion using FFmpeg to create .flac audio and normalize to 16 kHz mono
Large-file handling by splitting oversized audio files while preserving timestamps
Speech-to-text transcription with Groq Whisper (whisper-large-v3-turbo) and caching transcript JSON locally
Chunking transcript segments into overlapping text chunks with metadata (text, start/end time, source file, index)
Embedding generation using sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2)
Vector database indexing in Qdrant with payload index on source field and deterministic UUIDs
Semantic search and Q&A by embedding user query, retrieving top‑k chunks, and using Groq LLM to generate answers grounded in retrieved context with timestamps
